One person looking.
Everyone else joining.

Ya Selva is the artist. Break This Loop is what happens after he leaves. This is how they connect.

↓  SCROLL
The character

A modern bard
with a sampler

He travels looking for what's actually true — in a world of machines, advertisements and noise, he's trying to find where the real human heart is. He is not building anything. He's looking.

Everywhere he goes he records: field samples, street sounds, local players, his own voice. Then he makes songs out of what he found. The collecting and the singing are the same act — the journey is the source material.

Archetype
Explorer · Traveler Not sage, not magician. He goes and finds out.
Lineage
Alan Lomax × Xavier Rudd Paul Simon and Walt Whitman with an Ableton Push. Graceland is the template: travel, record real players in their own idiom, then write your own songs from it.
Carries
Sampler · acoustic guitar · charango · voice Moss on the machine. The drum with wires around it. Organic and electronic were never opposites — that's the whole argument, made as an object.
Truth check
Close enough to be honest Every element is documented behavior: 200+ gatherings led, street performance, the night the car broke down and he ran it on voice alone. Volume turned up, not invented.
What keeps happening

He doesn't build
community. It forms.

He plays under a bridge for nobody. Ten people stop. They sing. Next month there are thirty. Five people in a creek became a hundred and fifty in two months — nobody planned that. It accreted around someone doing the thing.

That's the engine, and it's already been proven once at small scale: gathering → community → audience → band → headline. The character doesn't need a strategy. He needs to keep showing up.

The handoff

He leaves.
It keeps going.

Moonlight needs him in the room. Ya Selva needs him on stage. Break This Loop is defined by running without him.

That's the whole distinction. Not earthy versus urban — present versus absent. What he collects becomes the material everyone else gets to build from, in every city, all year, whether or not he's there.

The place

Break This Loop is
not his aesthetic.

An artist has a sound. A platform hosts many. Ya Selva is forest green and lamp light. Break This Loop is black ink on cheap paper, pasted on a wall, in every language. Burning Man doesn't sound like its founders.

Its identity comes from everyone in it — already 20+ countries, six continents. He's the first contributor, not the owner. A participant isn't a brand. A participant is proof.

BTL // 001 — rooted in culture, driven by sound

The system — one voice, many faces

Three things, one night

How they stack

01

Ya Selva

The artist you follow · presence required

The character, the songs, the set. Exists with or without Break This Loop — street corners, releases, his own cult following. This is the one where he's the artist and not the infrastructure. Guard it.

02

Moonlight

The gathering you attend · presence required

Monthly, wherever he is. Circle, breakout rooms, closing share, community jam — then he plays. The workshop is the opening act, which is why the room sings by the time the set starts. Already proven: five people to a hundred and fifty.

03

Break This Loop

The project you contribute to · runs without him

The archive, the remix cycle, the global rituals a couple of times a year. Every Moonlight feeds it. So do the documentary tours and the online submissions. It gets bigger the longer it runs — it doesn't need to be maximally impressive on day one.

One night, in order

The run of show

Recording happens inside the experience, never as a filming session. Nobody is being filmed — they're having a night that happens to be captured.

Doors

Arrive early

The opt-in tier. Capped at the room — around thirty.

45 min

The circle

Small groups, tonight's theme, real questions. People connect with each other first.

60–90 min

Breakout rooms

Three or four producers, three or four spaces. People express on the theme. This is the capture.

15 min

Come back

Short closing share. Be witnessed.

The set

Ya Selva plays

The room isn't an audience. It's the people who just made something together, now being celebrated — with footage from every previous city woven through the show.

Next week

The pieces drop

Contributors paired with collaborators elsewhere in the world. They look like legends, because they're standing next to musicians from six continents.

Non-negotiable

The rules that
keep it alive

01
The night is the atom. Everything else is downstream of one night existing.
02
The performance is the draw. Without the set it's a filming session people attend as a favor. Never cut the show.
03
Capture and turnaround are somebody else's job. If he's running the room and managing the shoot, the model already failed.
04
Use the warm start. Never let one scene be the only channel — make node two deliberately different.
05
Seeding is legitimate. Pretending it's arriving live isn't. The honest version is stronger social proof.
06
Credit, consent, compensation designed in from day one — that's what separates the record people love from the one people litigate.
07
Historic accumulates. It doesn't arrive. Whitacre opened with 185 singers from 12 countries.

Ya Selva collects. The songs are what the journey makes.
Break This Loop is what happens when everyone else gets to do the same thing.
